ops.title: Remote access is HTTPS-only: self-signed pinned LAN leg, loopback-only HTTP plane
ops.body: Security review found the pair bearer token crossing the LAN in cleartext (daemon bound 0.0.0.0, pair advertised http:// URLs). Fix (commits c54f8bc, 2da5349): the plain-HTTP plane never leaves loopback; remote access rides TLS extra listeners only — a persisted self-signed ECDSA cert (`~/.cc-runtime/lan-cert.pem`, minted race-safe via exclusive link like the token) served on every interface at fixed port 25444 (`access.LANTLSPort`), beside the tailscale-cert leg on 25443. The pair payload gained `fp` (SHA-256 of the leaf DER, hex) so native clients authenticate the LAN leg by pinning; browsers hit a one-time self-signed interstitial. `access.Config.Bind` ("0.0.0.0") is now purely the persisted remote-access switch — the daemon's BindAddr stays zero/loopback. pair restarts any daemon whose handshake shows a non-loopback bind (legacy cleartext) or a TLS-leg count mismatch. Bonjour advertises 25444. Known limitation: a browser on the self-signed LAN leg cannot register the service worker (untrusted cert is not a secure context), so Web Push works only via the tailnet leg — equally true of the old cleartext leg; the pinned-fp path is for the native (iOS, P3) client.
